title: One-dimensional quantum Gibbs states in constant circuit depth
authors: Saúl Pilatowsky-Cameo, Georgios Styliaris, Ainesh Bakshi, Daniel Malz
abstract: We prove that the Gibbs state of any spin chain can be exactly decomposed into a mixture of product states over contiguous blocks of qubits with bounded length, at any constant temperature. As a consequence, any such Gibbs state can be prepared by local unitary circuits of constant depth, with efficient classical preprocessing. We place strong limits on the spatial structure of thermal entanglement: both the entanglement depth and entanglement width (measures of multiparticle entanglement) are bounded by constants, while the localizable entanglement (the bipartite entanglement that can be generated with the aid of local measurements and classical communication) vanishes exactly beyond a constant threshold distance. Our result also has implications for quantum thermalization: for any translation-invariant spin-chain Hamiltonian with nondegenerate spectral gaps, typical low-complexity pure states drawn from a maximally entropic ensemble at any constant effective temperature become locally indistinguishable from the Gibbs state upon unitary evolution. Additionally, we obtain an analogous decomposition for fermionic systems: the Gibbs state of any 1D local fermionic Hamiltonian is exactly a mixture of constant-depth local fermionic circuits acting on Gaussian states.
summary: This work characterizes the structure of quantum Gibbs states in 1D systems, showing they are highly structured and can be prepared efficiently using only constant-depth quantum circuits. The findings establish strong bounds on entanglement, demonstrating that long-range localizable entanglement vanishes rapidly in 1D at finite temperatures. This has significant implications for understanding quantum thermalization dynamics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the structural properties and resource requirements for preparing quantum Gibbs states at thermal equilibrium in one-dimensional systems.
main_result: It proves that 1D Gibbs states can be decomposed into mixtures of product states over bounded blocks, allowing preparation via quantum circuits of constant depth.
method: The authors use mathematical decomposition techniques, relating the Gibbs state to local operators and employing concepts from entanglement theory to establish separability bounds.
model_or_system: The focus is on 1D spin chains (qubits) and fermionic systems governed by geometrically local Hamiltonians, analyzed at constant positive temperatures.
key_observables: Entanglement depth, entanglement width, localizable entanglement, and circuit depth complexity.
important_parameters: Constant temperature ($ eta$ fixed), 1D geometry, and the constant depth bound $C_ eta$ which depends on $ eta$.
main_assumptions: The Hamiltonian is geometrically local, and the results are proven for constant positive temperatures.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates the construction involving Entanglement Bulk Decomposition (EBD) and the factorization of the state operator $\Omega$ over local regions.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the general decomposition of the Gibbs state (Theorem 1) to proving its preparation via constant-depth circuits (Corollary 1), analyzing entanglement bounds (Corollary 2), and extending these results to fermionic systems and quantum thermalization.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous, resource-theoretic bounds on the entanglement structure of thermal states, which is crucial for understanding how quantum information is stored and processed in realistic, interacting many-body systems.
